s1.text: Monday. Your AI agent saves a report. Company revenue: five thousand, five hundred sixty-five dollars. Tuesday, someone corrects the euro exchange rate. The report doesn't change. Nothing tells it that it's wrong.

s2.text: Agents build on their own saved work, so every number quietly depends on inputs underneath. When one input changes, which numbers are now wrong? Re-reading everything floods the model with context. Searching for related text misses numbers that depend on the change but never mention it.

s3.text: ProofFlow takes a different path. Every number keeps its receipts: exactly which inputs, and which calculation, made it. So it knows what to hold back, and what to redo.

3b.text: Every number keeps its receipts: exactly which inputs, and which calculation, made it.

3c.text: So it knows what to hold back, and what to redo.

s4.text: An input, like the exchange rate, is saved as a version. A tool reads it, and leaves a receipt. The receipt points to its result, and each number in a report points to that result. Now, correct the rate. The change travels up those links. Both revenue figures are withheld, never shown stale. Support never read the rate, so it stays. Refresh re-runs only the affected steps.

s5.text: This is ProofFlow, running today. Upload orders as a CSV, preview them, and create the reports. Publish a corrected rate. Affected figures are withheld, and the evidence path shows why. Refresh brings them current, and a checked report can only be copied while every figure is current. Agents get the same power, through five MCP tools.

s6.text: Under the hood, it's small, and strict. At the center is the runtime. Every tool run produces an immutable result, and a receipt. Content goes into a store that verifies every hash. Relationships go into HydraDB, as a lineage graph. When a correction arrives, HydraDB walks that graph natively, to find everything downstream. The runtime re-runs stale steps in order, reuses what's current, and records new receipts. If evidence is missing, it fails closed. No fallback. No guess. Around it: a browser app, a Python API, and an MCP server. Agents choose plans from typed tools, but never run arbitrary code.

s7.text: Does it work? In a frozen study with a real model, ProofFlow refreshed all thirty-two affected reports, matching full context at under forty percent of its input. Keyword search managed twenty-five. Vector search, five. On a retail benchmark: thirty-eight of thirty-eight, with sixty-nine percent fewer evidence tokens. A plain dependency walk ties it. The point is recording dependencies.
